title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?

input.lead: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
input.summary: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
input.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

input.lead: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
input.summary: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
input.evidence_text: Manchester Airport warns passengers ahead of busy bank holiday - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Passengers are being warned not to pack items powered by lithium batteries in hold bags By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 28 August 2026 Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history. The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk. It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them. About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator. 'Catch fire without warning' Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage. "If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said. Shaw said staff could screen almost 1,000 bags for a large long-haul aircraft and several hundred for a short-haul flight. "Each bag that fails to pass security checks gets pulled aside, and often needs to be inspected manually," he said. "This can create delays, but it also creates a risk that your hold bag might not make it onto the plane at all." The CAA said a fire on board could result in an aircraft being diverted or evacuated. Vapes, power banks and spare batteries must be carried in the cabin rather than placed in checked baggage. title: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors

input.lead: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
input.summary: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
input.evidence_text: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors - BBC News Image source, Bolton Council Image caption, The festival began in 2005 and is the biggest food and drink festival in England By Paul Burnell North West Published 28 August 2026 More than half a million people are expected to attend Bolton's Food and Drink Festival as over 100 food vendors will serve up tasty meals and drinks over four days. Big name chefs include James Martin, Marco Pierre White and Nisha Katona will serve up cooking demos. The festival site is spread across the town centre and organisers suggest Victoria Square information point is the best place for visitors to collect a free guide to help plan their day. Debbie Newall, Bolton Council's executive cabinet member for culture, said: "This is an opportunity to support local traders, celebrate fantastic food and drink, and showcase the very best of Bolton." "From artisan stalls and celebrity chef demonstrations, to live music and family activities, there is something for everyone to enjoy. "We are so proud of the continued success of the festival, and I urge everyone to visit and show their support." Free events taking place include street performers, children's activities, live music and entertainment throughout the weekend including headliners Liberty X and The Real Thing with demonstrations from regional chefs at Victoria Square. Meanwhile interactive experiences across the festival site include circus skills workshops, giant doodle walls, bubble performances, creative art sessions and a giant sandpit. title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans

input.lead: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
input.summary: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
input.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 28 August 2026 Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. It marks the first time in professional football that a fan has designed a kit using AI tools. PUMA AI Creator is a custom generative AI tool that turns written prompts into kit designs within seconds – with no design experience required. Fans from over 200 countries brought forward their vision for what the third kit should look like, resulting in over 180,000 unique shirts. Following 1.7 million platform ratings, the most popular kits were shortlisted to the final 10, which went to fan vote in January 2025. With votes having been submitted by the club’s global fanbase, the winner was crowned: a white base split by a central two-tone sash, half sky blue, half navy, running the length of the shirt with a subtle gradient effect that shifts as it catches the light. Behind the winning kit was lifelong City fan Elliott. “City has been part of my life for as long as I can remember, so to have designed a kit that will now be worn by the players is a genuine honour,” he said. “I’ve always loved football shirts and design, and I created mine using PUMA AI Creator on my lunch break, never imagining it could actually become a City kit. “The whole experience has been incredible, from seeing people react to the design, to seeing it on the players for the first time when I was invited to the kit shoot.
